findings.evidence: "This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise."
findings.fix: Cite research, published case studies from other library systems, or documented precedent supporting the claim that patron behavior responds predictably to fine elimination across different library systems.
findings.location: Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide
findings.violation: The principle that patron response to fine elimination works universally across all library systems is asserted without backing via research, studies, precedents, or documented practice.

findings.evidence: "Thus, given the return-rate and avoidance-survey results above, the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year." The evidence is an 18-month pilot at 5 branches.
findings.fix: Either extend the evidence base beyond the 5-branch pilot (results from other similar library systems, additional pilots at other consortium branches), or qualify the recommendation as a proposed systemwide trial with defined success metrics and review points rather than a definitive implementation.
findings.violation: The central recommendation for systemwide elimination of fines across all ten branches is implemented with full certainty (effective at the next fiscal year) based on the strength of one internal pilot of 5 branches over 18 months, overstating the confidence the evidence warrants.

findings.evidence: "This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date; items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established."
findings.fix: Either provide data from the pilot showing that most returns occur within 60 days and this explains the 93 percent return rate, or revise the specification to a window explicitly supported by the pilot data or additional evidence.
findings.violation: The claim that the 60-day return window matches the return-rate pattern established by pilot data is asserted without evidence; the pilot data provided does not show or establish a 60-day timeframe.

findings.evidence: "A skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall the consortium has not planned for. The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring."
findings.fix: Address the objection directly: either identify the sources of materials-replacement funding the consortium will use to cover the lost fine revenue (budget reallocations, grants, alternative revenue sources), or explain why the revenue concern does not actually undermine the recommendation.
findings.violation: The section raises the revenue-shortfall objection but does not address it; the mention of the branch renovation project does not explain how the consortium will fund materials replacement or why the revenue concern is not a threat to the recommendation.
